/-!
# Conjecture 10.13

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Does there exist a *massive set* of independent elements in a free group $F_2$ on free
generators $a, b$, that is, a set $E$ of irreducible words on the alphabet
$a, b, a^{-1}, b^{-1}$ such that

1) no element $w \in E$ belongs to the normal closure of $E \setminus \{w\}$, and

2) the massiveness condition is satisfied:
$\overline{\lim}_{n \to \infty} \sqrt[n]{|E_n|} = 3$,
where $E_n$ is the set of all words of length $n$ in $E$?

Here $F_2$ is modelled as `FreeGroup (Fin 2)`, whose elements are exactly the irreducible
(freely reduced) words on $a, b, a^{-1}, b^{-1}$, and the length of the reduced word
representing $w$ is `FreeGroup.norm w`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.13» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ E : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 2)),
      (∀ w ∈ E, w ∉ Subgroup.normalClosure (E \ {w})) ∧
      atTop.limsup
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ ({w ∈ E | FreeGroup.norm w = n}.ncard : ℝ) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) = 3 := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Does there exist a *massive set* of independent elements in the free group $F_2$ on free
generators $a, b$, that is, a set $E$ of irreducible words on the alphabet
$a, b, a^{-1}, b^{-1}$ (i.e. a subset $E \subseteq F_2$) such that

1) no element $w \in E$ belongs to the normal closure of $E \setminus \{w\}$, and

2) the massiveness condition holds:
$\overline{\lim}_{n \to \infty} \sqrt[n]{|E_n|} = 3$,
where $E_n$ is the set of all words of length $n$ in $E$?

The sequence $\sqrt[n]{|E_n|}$ is bounded (since $|E_n| \le 4 \cdot 3^{n-1}$), so its
`limsup` in `ℝ` is the usual upper limit.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no existence question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ E ⊆ F_2 with both properties); items 1) and 2) are the defining conditions of 'massive set of independent elements', not separate questions — 1) says every w ∈ E lies outside the normal closure of E \ {w} (which in particular forces w ≠ 1), and 2) is a limsup over n of the n-th root of the count of elements of E of reduced word length n (in the free generators a, b) being exactly 3, the growth rate of F_2 itself (there are 4·3^{n-1} reduced words of length n, so the limsup is automatically ≤ 3); E is a set of freely reduced words, i.e. simply a subset of F_2, and |E_n| = 0 for some n is harmless under limsup.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates give the same mathematically correct encoding: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ E : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 2)) with (1) ∀ w ∈ E, w ∉ Subgroup.normalClosure (E \ {w}) and (2) Filter.limsup over atTop in ℝ of (ncard {w ∈ E | FreeGroup.norm w = n})^(1/n) = 3. Verified: FreeGroup.norm = toWord.length (reduced word length); each E_n is finite (≤ 4·3^(n-1) elements) so ncard is genuine; the sequence is bounded in [0,4] so the ℝ-lattice limsup is the classical upper limit; the n = 0 junk term equals 1 and is irrelevant; condition (1) is a conjunction (not an implication) and excludes w = 1 automatically. c04's Real.nthRoot agrees with rpow on nonneg inputs, so it is equivalent; c07's bespoke IsIndependent/IsMassive + API finiteness lemma is also correct but adds definitions that 'Keep the Lean simple' discourages. c06 chosen as the inline version with the most complete verbatim docstring (including the boundedness remark); it compiles with only the sorry warning.

where $E_n$ is the set of all words of length $n$ in $E$?

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.13» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ E : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 2)),
      (∀ w ∈ E, w ∉ Subgroup.normalClosure (E \ {w})) ∧
      atTop.limsup
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ ({w ∈ E | FreeGroup.norm w = n}.ncard : ℝ) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) = 3 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.13»

items: F_2 is modelled as `FreeGroup (Fin 2)`; the free generators a, b are `FreeGroup.of 0`, `FreeGroup.of 1`. A 'set of irreducible words' is taken to be simply a subset E of F_2, since elements of the free group correspond bijectively to reduced words (as the decomposition notes indicate).
Word length |w| is `FreeGroup.norm w` (length of the reduced word `w.toWord`), which is exactly the length of the irreducible word in the generators a, b.

|E_n| is `Set.ncard {w ∈ E | FreeGroup.norm w = n}`; the set is always finite (at most 4·3^(n-1) reduced words of length n), so `ncard` is the true cardinality and the `ncard = 0 for infinite sets` default is never reached.

The upper limit is `Filter.limsup … atTop` in ℝ with the n-th root written as `Real.rpow` `x ^ (1/(n:ℝ))`. The sequence is bounded in [0, 4], so the real-valued `limsup` (sInf of eventual upper bounds) coincides with the usual limsup; no EReal/ENNReal is needed. The n = 0 term evaluates to `x ^ 0 = 1` in Lean, which does not affect the limsup.

Condition 1 uses `Subgroup.normalClosure (E \ {w})` as a subgroup of `FreeGroup (Fin 2)`; membership `w ∉ …` is the literal statement. Since 1 lies in every subgroup, this automatically excludes w = 1, matching the notes.

Positive answer `answer(True)` means such a massive set of independent elements exists; the existential is placed after `answer(sorry)` per repository convention. Both defining conditions are conjoined (∧), not implications, avoiding the vacuous `∃ x, P x → Q` pitfall.

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; no candidate omitted it and no candidate objected to the decomposition. Modeling choices shared by all: F_2 = FreeGroup (Fin 2) (a = of 0, b = of 1); 'set of irreducible words' = subset of F_2; word length = FreeGroup.norm; normal closure = Subgroup.normalClosure of the set E \ {w} inside F_2; upper limit = Filter.limsup … atTop in ℝ; nth root = Real.rpow with exponent 1/n. Minor ambiguity: the source does not say whether E may contain the empty word, but condition 1) already forces 1 ∉ E since 1 lies in every normal closure. Reference URL uses arXiv v46 as given in the task source (existing Kourovka files cite v40); harmless. Final file is c06 unchanged.
